item.title: Doctor Couple Becomes Target Of A Delusional Killer Who Thinks They’re In A Love Triangle Together
item.description:
There are 2 younger women sitting around a table at a trap house in Dallas, Texas. They’re both Latina with a bit of baby fat in their cheeks - but they’re not just some college students looking to buy drugs.


 

They’re here to sell them – a lot of them.

 

One of the 2 women – she’s a narco with deep connections in Mexico. The other woman? Just a Spanish/English translator for her boss, the narco, and the dealer of the trap house, a man named Love.


 

They need someone to move product for them and since Love has connections in the US - this deal could mean a lump sum of drugs and cash PLUS a lifetime supply from the cartel.


 

He just needs to earn their trust. How?

Kill someone.

 

But not just anyone.

They already have the target picked out.

 

A 35 year old pediatric dentist named Kendra Hatcher.

Why would the cartels want to kill a random dentist for children in Dallas, Texas?

item.title: Cartel Boss Arrested in Influencer’s Live Killing, but Viewers Still Suspect Her BFF is Involved
item.description:
Destiny swapping is a widely debated topic. The idea that a person can somehow take your fate and swap it with theirs…is rooted in deep levels of jealousy. To the point that it can impact someone’s life and take their blessings, or so it’s believed.


 

It’s much more than a friend trying to dress like you or steal your partner. They are trying to latch onto who you are, your personality, your hopes and dreams. 


 

Some say that you can sense it happening. A person will insert themselves into your life, and all of a sudden you start to lose focus, you can’t even seem to make your own decisions. 


 

Valeria had no idea, but someone very close to her was seemingly jealous of her. Netizens believed that this person was so envious, that she’d kill Valeria to take her fate. 


 

This is the case of 23 year old Valeria Marquez 

And how she was shot and killed during a TikTok livestream.

item.description:
It's unclear who the saying "it can always be worse", is meant for.


 

A girl named Liv is suspicious that her boyfriend of 8 months is cheating on her.


 

But it can always be worse, right? But what if it's as bad as it can get? What if there is no worse… this is the bottom? Then what?


 

Liv reaches over while Mason sleeps. There is only one way to find out if he's cheating on her, go through his phone. Within the hour, she's packing her things and making a run for it.


 

What she found wasn't another woman. It was Mason negotiating prices with strangers on Telegram: $20 for videos, $30 for megalinks, $80 for all of the above. And links to what she later described to police as little girls between the ages of 6 and 7 years old, some as young as 3.


 

This is the case of Mason Hullo, a TikTok looksmaxxer exposed by his ex for purchasing CSAM, and his bizarre excuse behind why.

item.title: Drowning or Foul Play on Horn Island? Inside the Conflicting Stories in the Nolan Wells Case
item.description:
July 6th, at the northwestern tip of Horn Island, a body washes ashore face down in the water.


 

It’s the body of a missing 18-year-old, college football player Nolan Wells who disappeared after taking a boat with friends to celebrate the Fourth of July.


 

Since then, there have been more questions than answers. Witnesses share vastly different accounts of what happened on the island with Nolan. Some of his friends shut down their social media, some opt to do interviews, and some quietly post tributes on Instagram.


 

But Nolan Wells’ loved ones are still looking for answers that investigators aren’t providing…

Were there things on his phone that were deleted from the day he went missing?

If he stayed behind on the island, why didn’t he have his phone or keys with him?

And what’s with this circulating audio that netizens swear they can hear people shouting, ‘Nolan’s freaking dead!’

item.title: 13 Year Old Realizes His Twin Brother Is A Killer In The Middle Of Interrogation
item.description:
A forensic DNA test usually scans about 20 fixed markers of DNA. It may take a few days but it’s enough to differentiate a suspect from the rest of the world with a near perfect level of certainty.


 

Except for identical twins.


 

It’s not a perfect analogy but think of DNA as a 3 billion letter book. Most people have about 20 chapters that are completely different. For identical twins, their entire book is identical except for about 8 typos. Not 8 different chapters, or sentences, not even 8 different words. 8 letter typos amongst 3 billion letters.


 

The technology to find these is only available at a handful of labs and costs hundreds of thousands, even millions of dollars. Thankfully, identical twin crime is rare.


 

Except for Ohio.


 

A woman who lives alone is raped and murdered in her own home, and the DNA left at the scene traces back to a set of identical twins.


 

Two 13 year old boys are the main suspects but which twin is innocent?

And which twin is guilty?
